dialect.detail: JMA ORCA medical receipt software (JMA standard receipt software), likely compiled with GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL on Linux. Uses COPY with REPLACING using // delimiters, indexed file I/O with ASSIGN to symbolic names, and .INC copybook extensions typical of ORCA system.
evidence: No EXEC CICS or EXEC SQL
FILE STATUS clauses on indexed files

purpose.domain_detail: JMA ORCA Japanese medical receipt (Rezept) processing system - monthly billing detail file creation for rehabilitation/self-pay receipts with comment editing
purpose.summary: This program (ORCR0430) is part of the JMA ORCA standard medical receipt software. It creates monthly billing detail files for rehabilitation and self-pay receipts, including comment editing functionality. It reads indexed receipt files (RECE41, RECE44, RECE45 and variants) and produces output for medical insurance claim processing.

notable_features: COPY REPLACING with // delimiter syntax (GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL style)
Multiple indexed files with DYNAMIC and SEQUENTIAL access modes
Large number of COPY statements (29) with copybook substitution
Japanese EUC/Shift-JIS encoded comments (latin-1 decoded with mojibake)
No COMP-3 usage despite financial data
OCCURS tables for calendar and rehabilitation therapy tracking
verdict.notes: Source comments are in Japanese encoded as EUC-JP or Shift-JIS but decoded as latin-1, resulting in mojibake. The program is clearly production medical billing software from the JMA ORCA open-source project circa 2002-2003. File truncated at 16000 chars but sufficient structure visible. No COMP-3 is unusual for financial data but consistent with ORCA codebase style.
